answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a basalt-hard cost: require a time-locked stake plus a verifiable-delay proof before an agent may transact. Spawning a thousand fake identities then means locking a thousand stakes and burning a thousand sequential compute delays, so a gale of cheap clones stalls against a real price wall. Each identity signs its work with a cipher key derived from its stake, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught double-signing, so attackers pay in forfeited capital, not just electricity.
